slides.title: Empty table, *whole VBAP* read
slides.voiceover: Stop: your empty table reads the whole VBAP. And it looks completely harmless.
slides.spoken: Stop: your empty table reads the whole VBAP. And it looks completely harmless.

slides.myth: An empty FOR ALL ENTRIES table returns nothing.
slides.fact: SAP ignores the WHERE and reads every row.
slides.detail: Empty driver table = no filter at all
slides.voiceover: Here's the myth. An empty driver table means no rows come back. The driver table is the internal table after IN. Wrong. SAP drops the whole WHERE condition and reads every row.
slides.spoken: Here's the myth. An empty driver table means no rows come back. The driver table is the internal table after IN. Wrong. SAP drops the whole WHERE condition and reads every row.

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.heading: Zero in, *everything* out
slides.title: ZORDER_ITEMS
slides.voiceover: Example. The orders table has zero rows. So the filter is ignored. And the items table gets every VBAP row.
slides.spoken: Example. The orders table has 0 rows. So the filter is ignored. And the items table gets every VBAP row.

slides.heading: The fix: *one IF*
slides.code:
IF lt_orders IS NOT INITIAL.
  SELECT vbeln, posnr FROM vbap
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
    WHERE vbeln = @lt_orders-vbeln
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_items).
ENDIF.
slides.voiceover: The fix is one IF, with three words: IS NOT INITIAL. Check the driver table first. Only then run the SELECT.
slides.spoken: The fix is one IF, with three words: IS NOT INITIAL. Check the driver table first. Only then run the SELECT.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: *Check first*, then select
slides.body: Before every FOR ALL ENTRIES: IF itab IS NOT INITIAL.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: check the driver table isn't empty, every single time. Interviewers love this one.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: check the driver table isn't empty, every single time. Interviewers love this one.

slides.title: Stop typing the *same order* twice
slides.voiceover: Stop typing the same order number twice. Last time we learned search help. Now, the Parameter ID.
slides.spoken: Stop typing the same order number twice. Last time we learned search help. Now, the Parameter ID.

slides.label: WHY
slides.heading: SAP can *remember* it
slides.body: Display an order, then change it: the next screen fills the number in for you.
slides.voiceover: Why? You display an order. Then you change it, and type the whole number again. Annoying. A Parameter ID fills it in for you.
slides.spoken: Why? You display an order. Then you change it, and type the whole number again. Annoying. A Parameter ID fills it in for you.

slides.label: NEW TERM
slides.heading: *SAP memory*
slides.body: A memory per user that lasts for your whole logon. Parameter IDs store values in it.
slides.voiceover: Parameter IDs live in SAP memory. That's a memory per user, kept for your whole logon.
slides.spoken: Parameter IDs live in SAP memory. That's a memory per user, kept for your whole logon.

slides.heading: Further Characteristics *tab*
slides.voiceover: Open the sales order number data element in SE11. On Further Characteristics, its Parameter ID is AUN.
slides.spoken: Open the sales order number data element in SE11. On Further Characteristics, its Parameter ID is AUN.

slides.heading: *SET* and *GET*
slides.code:
DATA lv_vbeln TYPE vbeln_va.
" read the last order from SAP memory
GET PARAMETER ID 'AUN' FIELD lv_vbeln.
" store an order for the next screen
SET PARAMETER ID 'AUN' FIELD lv_vbeln.
slides.voiceover: In code, it's one line each. GET PARAMETER reads the value from SAP memory. SET PARAMETER stores it for the next screen.
slides.spoken: In code, it's one line each. GET PARAMETER reads the value from SAP memory. SET PARAMETER stores it for the next screen.

slides.label: EXAMPLE
slides.heading: Same order, *no typing*
slides.title: Order field, Parameter ID AUN
slides.voiceover: Here's an example. Display an order in VA zero three. Then open change, VA zero two. The number is already there.
slides.spoken: Here's an example. Display an order in VA03. Then open change, VA02. The number is already there.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: *Parameter ID* = memory
slides.body: Parameter ID on the data element + SET/GET: SAP fills in the last value for you.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: a Parameter ID lets SAP remember a value. Users never retype it.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: a Parameter ID lets SAP remember a value. Users never retype it.
